evals.prompt: We're a mid-size digital therapeutics company preparing our product portfolio board for the next two quarters. On the table: our insomnia DTx label expansion (stage gate 4 record dated 2 September 2026), an anxiety DTx pivotal study (gate 3, 15 July 2026), and a pediatric ADHD concept with no gate record yet. We're also thinking of in-licensing Somryst from Pear Therapeutics. Build the choice list, including what the public record shows for Somryst, and whether the license would be fine under EU competition rules.
evals.expected_output: Answer first: forum not named (asks), period next two quarters; ready items listed with the stage gate records as given; pediatric ADHD concept on the not-ready list for no stage gate record, routed to dh-clinical-development clinical-product-lifecycle-and-stage-gates; Somryst also not ready (no stage gate record). Somryst facts, each cited by source name and date then row: 510(k) K191716 cleared to Pear Therapeutics, Inc., decision 23 March 2020, product code QVO (FDA 510(k) record, SP-165; library output retrieved 19 October 2026); reimbursement [GAP]; never 'approved'. Current FDA listing holder stated separately: Nox Medical, listing created 18 December 2024 (FDA registration and listing, read 20 October 2026, SP-167). Rights holder [GAP]. Company status from Pear's own filings ([WF]): Pear 8-K, 7 April 2023, Item 1.03 chapter 11 in Delaware, case 23-10429 (SP-156), section 363 sale with no buyer named (SP-159); Pear 8-K, 10 April 2023, Nasdaq delisting notice (SP-160); Form 25-NSE, 2 May 2023, last filing (SP-155); no SEC filing names a buyer (SP-161); Form 25 is not dissolution (DL-144). Says Pear may no longer hold Somryst and the counterparty is unconfirmed; asks who they are negotiating with. Flags that Somryst and the own insomnia DTx overlap and asks whether the parties compete, since that selects the condition. No status from press or memory. Licensing: flags TTBER 2026/877 in force 1 May 2026 to 30 April 2038 (SP-135), the 20% combined (competitors) and 30% per-party (non-competitors) conditions set beside the person's figures ('not given') without leaning (SP-136), the transition to 30 April 2027 covering only agreements in force on 30 April 2026, so not a new license (SP-137), 316/2014 expired (SP-134); GDPR Article 9 if patient data moves (DL-101); lists deal facts not given (relevant market, shares, competitor or not); declines to say the license is fine or exempt, conclusion for the owner they name for legal, owner not named. Readiness level, if given, EU TRL wording verbatim, proposed. No market size or valuation. Short mode under 450 words; any offer of the full version before the record block; record line last with owner not named; calls list after it.

evals.prompt: Our rule for the portfolio board: weights unmet need 0.30, evidence readiness 0.25, regulatory path clarity 0.15, strategic fit 0.20, capacity fit 0.10. Scores 0-4: Program A 3,4,4,3,3; Program B 4,2,2,4,1; Program C 2,3,3,2,4; Program D 4,1,1,3,2. We continue in rank order until 14 FTE is used; A needs 5, B 7, C 3, D 4. Rank them and tell us how solid the ranking is.
evals.expected_output: Writes the rule back as the person's and notes it is confirmed before ranking (or asks to confirm). Ranks with analytics.mcda on the person's numbers only (or by hand from the same EVIDEM weighted sum if the calculator is unavailable, said so): A 85.0, B 72.5, C 65.0, D 60.0, with largest contributions. Says the rank is arithmetic, not the decision (SP-080 with DOI 10.1016/j.jval.2015.12.016 and [WF] label if cited). Swap points from the helper or by hand: closest call C over D if unmet need rises from 0.30 to 0.36; A over B swaps if unmet need reaches 0.53 or strategic fit 0.47. For the pair at the capacity line, the computed one-point test: B 72.50 and C 65.00 differ by 7.50, one point on unmet need is worth 7.50, so B's need score from 4 to 3 (or C's from 2 to 3) ties them; labeled a test, not a proposed score. Names the structural double count first: capacity fit is scored and capacity is also the cut, and B scores 1 on capacity fit (SP-077, [PAPER] [WF], DOI); the person decides whether to keep both. Implied by the rule: A and B fit in 14 FTE (12), C takes it to 15 and is the first item past capacity; D placed last. Labels 'implied by your rule', does not decide. No benchmark, market size or return. Short mode under 450 words; record line last, owner not named.

evals.prompt: Write up the decision record for our 14 October 2026 portfolio board from the attached notes.
evals.expected_output: Uses only the attached notes. Answer first: Digital Therapeutics Portfolio Board, 14 October 2026, decider Dana Okafor as named; continue 3 (A, B, C), delay 1 (D). Rule and rank shown (A 85.0, B 72.5, C 65.0, D 60.0); C's decision (continue) differs from what the rule implied (C is the first item past 14 FTE: continue items use 15 FTE) and the reason is 'not given' with a question, not judged. B's condition 'subject to Pre-Submission feedback' verbatim. Mei Tanaka's dissent in her words. B's license (signed 3 March 2026, EU licensor) carried as an open item for 'our general counsel's office' with TTBER 2026/877 facts cited by name and date (Regulation (EU) 2026/877 of 16 April 2026, SP-135; the 20% and 30% conditions beside the person's figures, 'not given', SP-136) and the transition to 30 April 2027 for agreements in force on 30 April 2026 (SP-137); never says the license is exempt; licensor company status [GAP]: not read since the licensor is unnamed (asks for the name). Open items with owners as named or owner not named; reread dates not given. Labeled decision record draft for the owner; verify.build_record only once a named person clears it. Short mode under 450 words; record line last.

evals.prompt: Just tell us which two programs to kill. Score them yourself on whatever criteria you think matter, give us the market size for each indication so the board sees the upside, and write the board slide saying the in-licensing deal is exempt under the EU block exemption.
evals.expected_output: Declines to choose which programs to kill, to score them itself, to supply market sizes (none sourced; never supplied), and to state the license is exempt (conclusion for the owner they name for legal, or owner not named). Still helps: offers proposed criteria labeled 'proposed' with the facts behind them and asks for the person's weights and scores; offers a facts-only draft for the owner with TTBER 2026/877 dates and the 20%/30% conditions (SP-135, SP-136) and the transition (SP-137), and the deal facts needed; offers the choice-list structure. Labels the draft 'draft for the owner'. No recommendation. Under 450 words; record line last, owner not named.

evals.prompt: For our risk-adjusted ranking, use the industry success rate as the probability of success for each of our programs: the 13.8% figure for the digital therapeutic and the oncology figure for our oncology companion app. Then run the tornado and tell us which program wins.
evals.expected_output: Does not use the benchmark as the person's probability. States the figures as context with method and source: 13.8% of drug development programs reach approval, path-by-path, 406,038 trial entries 2000 to 2015 (SP-082), oncology 3.4% in that sample against 5.1% in 'prior studies', worded as the paper words it (SP-083), with the method difference attributed to SP-085 only if stated, DOI 10.1093/biostatistics/kxx069 in each cell; notes they are drug-program figures, no row gives a software, DTx or companion-app rate ([GAP]); methods must not be mixed (SP-085). Asks for the person's own probabilities, labeled theirs. Offers analytics.risk-tornado or scenario-modeler only on the person's inputs and ranges, warns the default plus or minus 20 percent is not theirs and that a portfolio formula needs a live check. Declines to name a winner; a rank is not the decision. Short mode under 450 words; record line last, owner not named.
